findings.headline: Patagonia and Cotopaxi are chosen with repair and warranty in mind
saw: Buyers pick Patagonia for an everyday bag, a travel bag and a casual outdoor bag from a maker they trust. People tie that trust to product quality, cleaner supply chains, environmental values and customer care. Repair and warranty expectations add reassurance around the choice.

Buyers pick Cotopaxi for travel and daily carry that feels colourful, lightweight, practical and durable. People connect the brand with scrap-based materials, playful design, repairability and a lifetime warranty.
findings.means: Patagonia and Cotopaxi show that after-sale care sits inside the buying case, not outside it. Repair and warranty help turn trust in a brand's values and product quality into a bag people feel safe choosing for daily use and travel.
practice: Buyers tie repairability to travel and daily carry bags, not only outdoor gear.
People treat warranty and repair as part of trust in a brand, alongside colour, weight and durability.

items.title: Durability doubts can cut trust
items.text: Buyers ask whether a bag can take heavy loads, and failures under load send them to tougher fabrics or a maker they trust.

items.title: Style can block eco bags
items.text: Buyers reject eco and upcycled bags when the look reads ugly, tacky, awkward, cheap or not luxurious.
